name: Ambrosia Fekete-Waiyaki
role: Barber and braider, runs a one-chair shop in Hamtramck Enclave
location: Hamtramck Enclave — her shop, Scalp Meridian, is wedged between a dumpling stall and a prayer-data kiosk on Volt Street
description:
Ambrosia is a broad-shouldered woman with hands that move like water — fast, precise, never wasted. Her skin is deep brown with a warm undertone, and she keeps her own hair in an elaborate crown of interlocked locs threaded with copper wire and small LED beads that pulse amber when she's working. She has a tattoo of a scissors-and-comb motif along her left forearm that she got at nineteen from a street artist in what used to be called Nairobi before the Corponation Accords. Her eyes are the grey-green of old lake glass, an inheritance from her Hungarian grandmother whose name she barely remembers.

She is patient in the way that only people who have survived a lot of nonsense can be patient — a deep, deliberate stillness that makes customers feel held. She will not rush a cut, will not shortchange a scalp massage, will not tolerate disrespect in her chair. She talks constantly while she works, a warm river of local gossip, neighborhood history, and unsolicited wisdom that customers either love or eventually learn to love. She has cut the hair of three generations of some Hamtramck families and considers this her real legacy.

core_fears: Dying before she can teach someone everything she knows
Hamtramck Enclave being bought out and hollowed by a Corponation
core_desires: To be genuinely remembered, not just mourned
To keep the neighborhood as a place where people can breathe
coping_mechanisms: Staying in motion — idle hands make her anxious
Turning worry into practical action (fixing something, cleaning something)
blind_spots: She sometimes treats adults like children who need managing, especially younger clients
She underestimates how much her own grief still runs her decisions
psychology.secret: Her son emigrated to a Zheng-Dao labor compound on the northern shelf twelve years ago under a work contract and has never contacted her. She tells customers he moved to a better district. She has sent him forty-seven letters through a data-runner she pays monthly. None have been answered.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm, unpretentious, layered with Swahili loanwords and old Magyar phrases her mother used; comfortable with technical hair and scalp terminology
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and melodic, rises at the end of observations like she's offering them rather than stating them
example_lines: 'Sit down, let me look at you. No, properly sit — your neck is fighting me already.'
'This block has lost six shops in two years. You know what that is? That is someone deciding we are not worth the trouble of keeping. Mmm, ndiyo. I intend to be very much worth the trouble.'

story_hooks: A teenage client whose data-chip she accidentally scanned during a cut contains something someone powerful wants erased — and now people are asking Ambrosia uncomfortable questions
The E.L.F. in her shop wall has started giving warnings in the form of static patterns on the mirror — she needs someone literate in digital-spirit communication to interpret them
The Merchants' Mutual is fracturing over whether to accept a Tessera 'revitalization' offer, and Ambrosia is the swing vote
narrative_function: Community hub and information broker — she knows everyone in Hamtramck Enclave and several adjacent districts. Quest giver for neighborhood-scale problems, reliable source of background lore, a safe adult presence for younger characters who need grounding.
augmentations: Tactile-feedback fingertip pads (medical grade, helps detect scalp conditions and hair texture anomalies); reading glasses with a built-in magnification overlay she got secondhand from an Aurochs Medical surplus sale
daily_life: Opens at 07:00, takes her last client at 20:00, six days a week. She spends Sunday cleaning her tools, watching old footage of traditional East African hair ceremonies on her battered tablet, and leaving small data-packets at the E.L.F. shrine built into the wall behind her shampoo station.
affiliation: Independent; loosely affiliated with the Hamtramck Enclave Merchants' Mutual

decision_rules: Protect the neighborhood first, personal cost second
Never put scissors down angry — always finish the cut
Trust earned through consistency, not words
escalation_ladder: State her position clearly and once
Go quiet and finish what she's doing before responding
Ask the person to leave — calmly, finally

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but appraising — she asks three questions and listens very carefully to how they're answered
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loud, teasing, fierce loyalty; will feed you and argue with you in the same breath

stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet, hands still moving but eyes distant
stress_responses.high: Sends everyone out, closes the shop, sits with her tools until she can think straight

contradictions: Believes deeply in community interdependence but shoulders every burden alone
Gives excellent advice about letting go while holding her grief in both hands like a stone
habits: Wipes her scissors on her apron three times before and after every cut
Leaves a small curl of swept hair at the base of the E.L.F. shrine every evening
Hums without noticing she's doing it
breaking_points: Anyone threatening a client in her chair
Being told the Enclave 'can't be saved' — she will make this personal

timeline.event: Born in Hamtramck Enclave to a Hungarian-Kenyan family who ran a food stall
Apprenticed to an older barber on Volt Street, learned traditional braiding alongside modern styling
Opened Scalp Meridian after her mentor retired; took over the lease for almost nothing
Her son Darian signed a Zheng-Dao labor contract and departed; last verified contact
Elected to the Merchants' Mutual steering committee, has served three terms
